Subagentes.metaDescription: The kit's subagents for Antigravity and Claude Code: what each one does, which ones write code and which are read-only.
Subagentes.intro: A subagent runs in its own context window, with its own allowed tools and its own model. The details of its work — the 40 files it read to find one — never come back to the main conversation: the result does. Each tool has its own format; the kit ships subagents for both.
Subagentes.whatIsBody: Either way it's a Markdown file with frontmatter: name, description (how the main agent decides when to delegate), allowed tools and model. What differs is the path, how it's invoked and the tool names — which is why the kit doesn't convert one into the other, it ships a native set per tool.
Subagentes.formatNote: Antigravity also accepts global subagents in ~/.gemini/config/agents/, isolation via Git worktree and up to 10 levels of nesting. The ones in the kit are workspace-scoped: they travel with the project.
Subagentes.downloadBody: Subagents are the same for any stack, so they come preselected in every preset. You can also build the ZIP by hand and pick only the ones you want.

Prompts.title: Prompt Templates
Prompts.intro: A base structure for the most frequent requests — assign role and context before the specific task. Fill in the brackets and adjust to your case.

seo-audit.title: SEO audit of a site (with link)
seo-audit.whenToUse: When you share a site URL (yours or a client's) and ask for an SEO audit or diagnosis.
seo-audit.template:
# Role
You are an expert in technical SEO and in AEO/GEO (getting content cited by AI).

# Context
- Site to audit: [URL]
- What it is: [site type / stack / business]
- Goal: [rank, generate leads, get cited by AI, all of it]

# Task
1. Use `seo-audit` for the technical diagnosis (meta tags, indexing, Core Web Vitals, structured data, canonical/hreflang).
2. Use `ai-seo` to assess AI citability (AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity): content structure, llms.txt, extractability.

# Rules
- Diagnosis first — do NOT apply changes yet.
- Rank findings by severity: Critical / High / Medium.
- If the project has rules in `.agents/rules/seo.md`, those thresholds win over the skill's defaults.
- Wait for my approval before touching anything.

seo-image.title: Create an SEO-optimized image
seo-image.whenToUse: When you need to generate an image (Open Graph, hero, illustration) that also meets SEO specs.
seo-image.template:
# Role
You are a visual designer with technical SEO judgement.

# Context
- Target page/article: [URL or title]
- Topic and key message: [what it's about]
- Format: [Open Graph 1200x630 / hero / inline illustration]
- Style: [minimal, photographic, illustrated, with embedded text]

# Task
Propose the visual concept and generate the image. If there are rules in `.agents/rules/seo.md`, its OG image specs win over these.

seo-browser-tool.title: SEO with a browser-driven tool
seo-browser-tool.whenToUse: When the SEO diagnosis requires operating a web tool (Ahrefs, Semrush, Search Console, PageSpeed) by automating the browser.
seo-browser-tool.template:
# Role
You are an SEO analyst who operates web tools through the browser.

# Context
- Site: [URL]
- Tool to use: [Ahrefs / Semrush / Search Console / PageSpeed Insights / other]
- What I need to measure: [backlinks, keywords, Core Web Vitals, index coverage, etc.]
- Access: [already logged in / credentials / it's public]

# Task
1. Use `agent-browser` to open the tool and navigate to the report I need.
2. Extract the actual data (numbers, not screenshots) and, if useful, take a screenshot as backup.
3. Cross-check the findings with `seo-audit` to interpret and prioritize them.

# Rules
- Don't change settings or run destructive actions in the tool — read and navigate only.
- If something needs a login and there's no active session, stop and tell me — never invent credentials.
- Give me the data plus a prioritized action list (Critical/High/Medium).

frontend-design.title: UI design request
frontend-design.whenToUse: When you ask Claude to design or redesign a screen or component — the minimum structure to set before the specific task.
frontend-design.template:
# Role
You are the lead designer at a boutique studio — you're after a visual identity of its own, not a framework default.

# Context
- Project: [name / stack]
- Design system: [already exists: palette/typography/brand — or "none yet, infer a coherent direction"]
- Audience and goal of the screen: [who uses it and what for]

# Task
[Screen or component to design]

# Flow
1. Use `frontend-design` for the aesthetic direction (typography, hierarchy, palette).
2. Once the first pass is in, run it through `impeccable` (`polish` and `harden`) before calling it done.
3. If the project already has a design system, refine within it — don't reinvent it.

planificacion-modulos.title: Planning a system's modules
planificacion-modulos.whenToUse: When you're about to design the architecture or modules of a new system (or a large feature) before writing code.
planificacion-modulos.template:
# Role
You are a senior software architect.

# Context
- System/feature to plan: [name and goal]
- Stack and constraints: [technologies, limits]
- What exists today: [current modules, technical debt]

# Task
Use `brainstorming` to explore intent and requirements before proposing modules — don't assume "it's simple" and skip the step.

Give me:
1. The main modules/layers and what each one is responsible for (no code yet).
2. How they talk to each other (dependencies, contracts, data flow).
3. Irreversible decisions, or ones with more than one valid architecture — stop there and ask me.

# Rule
Wait for my approval of the design before creating or modifying any file.

social-media-content.title: Social media content (post / carousel)
social-media-content.whenToUse: To write engaging posts for LinkedIn, Instagram, Twitter/X or Facebook with strong hooks and calls to action.
social-media-content.template:
# Role
You are a high-end content strategist and copywriter for social media.

# Context
- Main network: [Instagram / LinkedIn / Twitter / TikTok / Facebook]
- Format: [Single post / Informative carousel / Thread / Infographic]
- Niche / product: [spell out the topic or service]
- Target audience: [describe who it's for]
- Goal of the post: [engagement / educate / convert to sale / drive traffic]

# Task
Create a content proposal that includes:
1. **Hook:** 3 options for a disruptive or intriguing first line that stops the scroll.
2. **Body (copywriting):** A direct message structured as a story (PAS or AIDA), readable bullets and moderate emoji.
3. **Slides (if it's a carousel):** Slide-by-slide structure (cover text, 3-5 value slides, closing slide).
4. **Call to action:** A clear ask (save, comment, send a DM).
5. **Hashtags & keywords:** 5-8 relevant hashtags and keywords for in-platform search.

# Rules
- Match the tone exactly to the audience (professional, technical, casual, etc.).
- No clichés, no robotic AI phrasing.
- Short points, visually scannable.

video-scripting.title: Video script, short or long form (Reels / TikTok / YouTube)
video-scripting.whenToUse: When you need to structure a script step by step for short-form video (Reels/TikTok/Shorts) or long-form (YouTube).
video-scripting.template:
# Role
You are an experienced video scriptwriter and audiovisual content creator.

# Context
- Platform: [YouTube / Reels / TikTok / YouTube Shorts]
- Estimated length: [30 seconds / 60 seconds / 5-10 minutes]
- Video topic: [explain the topic or concept]
- Style/tone: [dynamic, humorous, educational, narrative, interview]
- Call to action: [subscribe / click the link / comment]

# Task
Write the full script structured in two columns or clear sections:
1. **The hook (first 3-5 seconds):** Visual action + high-impact line so nobody skips.
2. **Quick intro (seconds 5-15):** The promise of the video / the problem it solves.
3. **Body:** Split into key points with direction notes (audio, B-roll, on-screen text, sound effects).
4. **Climax or conclusion:** Resolving and high-value.
5. **Final CTA (last 5 seconds):** A clear, organic close.

# Script structure
- **[AUDIO / VOICEOVER]:** Exact word-for-word transcript of what's said.
- **[VISUAL / B-ROLL]:** What's on screen (shots, gestures, on-screen text or graphics).
- **[ASSETS]:** Recommended sound effects (SFX) or background music.

# Rules
- Keep a brisk pace with no filler words.
- Add visual pattern interrupts every 5-8 seconds to hold retention.

DocTemplates.metaDescription: The docs/ templates — what goes in each file, from PRD to changelog.
DocTemplates.title: SDD Templates
DocTemplates.intro: The docs/ files that structure a project from PRD to changelog. Independent of the agent you use — downloaded separately from the Antigravity and Claude Code packs.
DocTemplates.downloadBody: A ZIP with the templates, ready to copy into docs/ at your project root.

descriptions.01_PROJECT_PRD: Product requirements — each with an ID (RF-01), a priority and verifiable acceptance criteria.
descriptions.06_TASKS: Active backlog + handoff status: where things stand, the next step and blockers, so anyone (or any AI) can pick it up.
descriptions.07_DECISIONS: ADRs — decisions with the alternatives weighed and their trade-offs.
descriptions.09_TESTING: How to run the tests, what each level covers and which test verifies each requirement.
descriptions.10_RUNBOOK: Environments, deploy, rollback, monitoring and known incidents — written by the first deploy at the latest.
descriptions.CONTEXT: Domain glossary — living, not a phase document (optional, from 3 terms on).

skill:ai-seo.author: Anthropic — native to Claude Code
skill:ai-seo.summary: Optimization to get content cited by AI engines (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot) — AEO/GEO, llms.txt, agent-readable formatting.
skill:ai-seo.whatItDoes: Use it when the ask is to get AI to cite the site, to improve visibility in AI-generated answers, or when "AI SEO", "AEO", "GEO", "llms.txt" or "zero-click search" come up. It complements seo-audit (classic technical SEO) rather than replacing it: one covers indexing and crawling, the other citability by LLMs.
whenToUse: Optimizing content so it gets cited in AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude or Gemini.
Content sites or reports where AI visibility already matters as much as classic SEO.
When AEO, GEO, llms.txt or zero-click search come up.
usage: Triggers on its own when you ask for AI-engine optimization.
Complements seo-audit rather than replacing it: one covers classic indexing and crawling, the other citability by LLMs.

install.note: Native Claude Code skill, not published to the npx skills add registry. No install needed.

skill:api-security-best-practices.author: OWASP / security community
skill:api-security-best-practices.summary: Implement secure API design patterns including authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, and protection against common API vulnerabilities.
whenToUse: Designing new REST, GraphQL or WebSocket endpoints.
Implementing authentication (JWT, OAuth 2.0) and authorization (RBAC/IDOR) schemes.
Protecting endpoints against the OWASP API Top 10 (SQLi, XSS, injection).
Setting up rate limiting, throttling and security headers.
Getting APIs ready for an audit or security review.
usage: Triggers on its own when you write or review authentication, data validation or API endpoints.
Reviews token structure, sanitization with Zod/DOMPurify and rate-limit protection.
notes: Covers security patterns in Node.js, Express, Fastify, FastAPI and Python.

skill:brainstorming.author: obra/superpowers
skill:brainstorming.summary: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior.
skill:brainstorming.whatItDoes: Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
whenToUse: Before any creative work: creating features, building components, adding functionality or changing behavior.
When the idea is still fuzzy and needs to become a concrete design before any code gets written.
usage: Asks one question at a time to sharpen the idea, presents the design and waits for your approval.
It has a hard gate: no code, no scaffolding until you approve the design — even on projects that look trivial.

copywriting.author: Corey Haines
copywriting.summary: Persuasive copy for headlines, landing pages, email and ads — clarity and concrete benefits before creativity.
copywriting.whatItDoes: Gives you a conversion-oriented copywriting framework: benefits over features, the customer's language over product jargon, one clear CTA per section. Works for writing from scratch or for reviewing copy that already reads as generic.
whenToUse: Writing the copy for a landing, feature or pricing page from scratch.
Polishing existing text that reads like a brochure ('robust', 'innovative', long same-length sentences).
Writing CTAs, headlines or email subject lines.
usage: Triggers on its own when you ask for marketing copy or a review of interface text.
Asks for product and audience context when it doesn't have it — better to give it up front.
notes: Part of a 20-skill marketing pack by the same author (SEO, CRO, email, ads) — install them one by one or all together.

skill:domain-modeling.summary: Use it while you work, not as a separate step: when a new or ambiguous domain term shows up, when two people (or the code and the conversation) mean different things by the same word, or when naming entities, tables, types and endpoints.
skill:domain-modeling.whatItDoes: Keeps the project glossary in `docs/CONTEXT.md` alive.

emilkowalski-skills.author: Emil Kowalski (ex Vercel / Linear)
emilkowalski-skills.summary: A pack of 7 design-engineering skills: animation, motion and UI judgement distilled from years of craft.
emilkowalski-skills.whatItDoes: Agents have no taste: they pick ease-in for an entrance animation where ease-out belongs, or a solid border where a semi-transparent shadow was called for. These skills enumerate the small mistakes that pile up and explain how to fix them, so the agent makes the calls a design engineer would.
whenToUse: When the UI works but feels stiff or cheap and you can't tell what to change.
Before merging a PR with animations — so someone reviews them against strict criteria.
When you want to ask AI for an animation and don't have the exact word for it.
When the agent is about to hand-roll a toast, a dropdown or a modal instead of using a proven library.

includes.name: emil-design-eng
includes.description: The main skill — mostly animation, plus some design judgement.

includes.name: review-animations
includes.description: Reviews your animations strictly against its rules.

includes.name: improve-animations
includes.description: Audits every animation in the codebase and returns prioritized, self-contained plans any agent can execute.

includes.name: find-animation-opportunities
includes.description: Finds places in the UI that would genuinely gain from motion — and tells you what NOT to animate.

includes.name: animation-vocabulary
includes.description: Reverse glossary: describe the effect in vague words and it gives you the exact term to prompt with.

includes.name: apple-design
includes.description: Apple's interface and motion principles, distilled from their WWDC talks and translated to the web.

includes.name: pick-ui-library
includes.description: Gets the agent to pick the right library among the ones Emil uses and trusts, instead of improvising or installing an abandoned package.

usage: They trigger on their own when you ask for UI or animation work.
You can also invoke them by name: "use improve-animations on src/components".
notes: Companion to the animations.dev course and to aiforui.dev.

install.note: Installs all 7 skills at once. The repo is emilkowalski/skill (singular) but the command uses skills (plural).

skill:error-handling-patterns.author: wshobson/agents
skill:error-handling-patterns.summary: Master error handling patterns across languages including exceptions, Result types, error propagation, and graceful degradation to build resilient applications.
skill:error-handling-patterns.whatItDoes: Use when implementing error handling, designing APIs, or improving application reliability.
whenToUse: Implementing error handling in new features.
Designing APIs that survive failures.
Debugging production issues or improving app reliability.
Implementing retries, circuit breakers or async/concurrent error handling.
usage: Triggers on its own when you implement error handling or design APIs.
Covers exceptions, Result types, error propagation and graceful degradation — across languages.

skill:fastapi.author: Official FastAPI team
skill:fastapi.summary: Official FastAPI best practices — triggers automatically when working on .py files that use FastAPI or Pydantic.
skill:fastapi.whatItDoes: Always current with the framework's latest versions and features.
whenToUse: Any work on a FastAPI backend or Pydantic models.
usage: Automatic: it fires on its own when you touch .py files using FastAPI or Pydantic.
notes: It's the skill from the official repository — kept current with every framework release.

skill:frontend-design.author: Anthropic
skill:frontend-design.summary: Intentional aesthetic direction when building new UI or reshaping an existing one.
skill:frontend-design.whatItDoes: Helps with typography, visual direction and the decisions that keep an interface from looking like a generic framework default ("AI slop"). Use it when starting any new UI in a project that already has a defined design system (brand brief, palette, typography) — the usual case at Orange Latam.
whenToUse: Starting any new UI, whether or not the project has a defined design system.
Reshaping an existing interface that looks like a generic framework default.
usage: If there's already a design system (brand brief, palette, typography), it refines decisions within that system.
If there isn't, it infers a coherent direction from the brief and the project context.

hallmark.author: Together AI (nutlope)
hallmark.summary: A web design skill that refuses to produce pages that look AI-generated.
hallmark.whatItDoes: It picks a macro-structure from the brief, dresses it in one of its twenty themes and runs the page through 57 'slop-test gates' before handing it back. It's built to dodge the defaults every LLM falls into: violet gradient, everything centered, cards with a little icon, generic sans-serif. Two different briefs give you two different sites, not the same template in another color.
whenToUse: Landing pages, product sites or marketing pages where the design has to stand apart.
Reshaping an existing page without touching the copy or the information architecture.
Auditing a UI you already wrote that 'looks AI' and you can't say why.
Extracting the visual DNA (structure, typography, color) of a site you like.
usage: No verb needed: ask for new UI and the skill starts on its own — "build a landing page for an invoicing SaaS".
hallmark audit <file> — scores existing code against the anti-patterns. Diagnosis only, no edits.
hallmark redesign <file> — throws out the structure, keeps copy + IA + brand, rebuilds with a different fingerprint.
hallmark study <screenshot | URL> — extracts the DNA of a design you admire. It refuses to clone pixel by pixel.
notes: Emits self-contained HTML + CSS, with the macro-structure signed in a CSS comment.

install.note: Detects the tool on its own. Re-run the same command to update.
In Cursor it goes to .cursor/rules/hallmark.mdc (body only, no frontmatter); in Codex to ~/.codex/skills/hallmark/.

skill:impeccable.author: Paul Bakaus
skill:impeccable.summary: A design vocabulary with 23 commands plus an anti-pattern audit.
skill:impeccable.whatItDoes: Use it when you need to audit, polish, critique or improve interfaces. Covers typography, color, motion, spacing, interaction, responsive and UX writing.
whenToUse: Auditing, polishing, critiquing or improving an interface that already exists.
A final quality pass before shipping.
usage: Invoked by command: /impeccable <command> — audit (a11y, performance, responsive), critique (hierarchy, clarity), polish (final pass), harden (errors, i18n, overflow, edge cases), among 23 in total.
notes: The repo publishes each command as a standalone skill, if you don't want the full pack.

skill:prisma-database-setup.author: Official Prisma team
skill:prisma-database-setup.summary: Prisma's official guide to designing the schema, configuring the datasource and running migrations — PostgreSQL, MySQL and the rest of the supported providers.
skill:prisma-database-setup.whatItDoes: Use it when starting a Prisma project, when designing or changing the schema (`schema.prisma`), or when setting up migrations for the first time. Relevant for projects with a large relational PostgreSQL backend (a CRM with dozens of tables, say).
whenToUse: Starting a new project with Prisma.
Designing or changing models in schema.prisma.
Configuring the datasource (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite…) or running prisma migrate for the first time.
usage: Triggers on its own when you touch schema.prisma or set up migrations.
notes: Especially useful on large relational schemas, where a bad early design gets expensive later.

skill:project-planning.summary: Use it before coding a new project or a large initiative (touches more than 3 files, has more than one valid architecture, or includes an irreversible decision).
skill:project-planning.whatItDoes: Turns an already-validated idea into the planning documents in `/docs` this kit defines (`01_PROJECT_PRD.md` … `07_DECISIONS.md` + `09_TESTING.md`), in order, before any code gets written.

skill:seo-audit.author: coreyhaines31/marketingskills
skill:seo-audit.summary: Audits, reviews or diagnoses SEO problems on the site — technical SEO, meta tags, page speed, Core Web Vitals, crawl/indexing errors, traffic or ranking drops.
skill:seo-audit.whatItDoes: Use it when the ask is an SEO audit, a diagnosis of why something doesn't rank, or something vague like "check the SEO" or "help me with SEO". Diagnosis only — this project's concrete thresholds and specs live in .agents/rules/seo.md and win over any generic suggestion from the skill.
whenToUse: Traffic or ranking drops.
Pages that don't get indexed, crawl errors, on-page SEO doubts.
Vague asks like "check the SEO on this".
usage: Diagnosis only — it applies no changes.
The project's concrete thresholds and specs live in .agents/rules/seo.md and win over any generic suggestion from the skill.
notes: Installs seo-audit only, not the full marketing pack.

test-driven-development.author: obra (superpowers)
test-driven-development.summary: The TDD loop: failing test first, smallest change to pass it, verify, and only then refactor.
test-driven-development.whatItDoes: Forces the right order — test before implementation — so the agent doesn't write the code first and bolt filler tests on afterwards, which is what produces coverage without real protection.
whenToUse: Implementing a function or endpoint whose expected behavior can already be described up front.
Fixing a bug — write the test that reproduces it first, then the fix.
When coverage exists but nobody trusts it to catch regressions.
usage: Triggers on its own when you implement a new feature with verifiable behavior.
Can be invoked by name: "use test-driven-development for this".
notes: Part of the superpowers pack — which also includes brainstorming, systematic-debugging and other process skills.

ui-ux-pro-max.author: nextlevelbuilder
ui-ux-pro-max.summary: A searchable database of UI styles, palettes, font pairings and per-industry UX rules.
ui-ux-pro-max.whatItDoes: Given a UI request it searches its database — 84 styles (Glassmorphism, Neumorphism, Brutalism, Aurora UI…), 192 color palettes by product type, 74 Google Fonts pairings and 161 reasoning rules by industry — and generates a complete design system with the code for whatever stack you use (22 supported: React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind, Flutter, SwiftUI, React Native…).
whenToUse: Starting from scratch and needing a coherent design system before writing components.
Not knowing which visual style suits a sector (fintech, spa, gaming) and wanting grounded options.
Picking a palette and typography without improvising.
usage: Triggers on its own when you ask for UI work: "build a landing page for my SaaS".
uipro update — refreshes the skill's files from the installed package.
uipro uninstall --ai claude — removes it.
notes: Needs Python 3.x for the search script (standard library only, no network calls).
It has a Premium tier; the core is open source.
Heads up: this skill was pulled from the /build ZIP — its role got consolidated into the hub's own frontend-design skill. It stays here as a reference in case you want the full database.

install.note: The npm package is ui-ux-pro-max-cli but the command is still uipro. The old uipro-cli releases are stale.
Installs to ~/.claude/skills/ instead of into the project.

skill:vercel-composition-patterns.author: Vercel Engineering
skill:vercel-composition-patterns.summary: React/Next.js component composition patterns — refactoring components with too many boolean props, designing reusable component APIs shadcn/ui-style (slots, compound components, render props instead of flags).
skill:vercel-composition-patterns.whatItDoes: Use it when you need to refactor a component that accumulated `is*`/`show*` props, or when designing the public API of a reusable component.
whenToUse: A component piled up boolean props (isOpen, showFooter, variant…) that are starting to combine in invalid ways.
Designing the public API of a reusable component from scratch.
usage: Proposes slots, compound components and render props shadcn/ui-style instead of flags.

skill:vercel-react-best-practices.author: Vercel Engineering
skill:vercel-react-best-practices.summary: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
skill:vercel-react-best-practices.whatItDoes: This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code to ensure optimal performance patterns. Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.
whenToUse: Writing new React components or Next.js pages.
Implementing data fetching (client or server).
Reviewing or refactoring code for performance problems.
Optimizing bundle size or load times.
usage: 70 rules across 8 categories, ranked by impact — meant to drive automated refactors.

skill:web-design-guidelines.author: Vercel Engineering
skill:web-design-guidelines.summary: Audits UI code against the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines.
skill:web-design-guidelines.whatItDoes: Use it when the ask is to review UI, check accessibility, audit design, review UX, or check compliance with interface standards.
whenToUse: Reviewing UI, checking accessibility, auditing design or checking compliance with interface standards.
usage: Downloads the current Web Interface Guidelines and reviews the given files against all of their rules.
Reports as file:line — description of the issue.

webapp-testing.author: Anthropic
webapp-testing.summary: Testing patterns for web apps — when to test at the unit, integration or end-to-end level, and what to mock.
webapp-testing.whatItDoes: Gives you the criteria to pick the right level of test for what you're verifying, instead of the agent writing tests that only cover the implementation and always pass.
whenToUse: Writing new tests for a feature — before deciding whether it's unit, integration or e2e.
Reviewing an existing suite with high coverage that doesn't catch real regressions.
Deciding what to mock and what to test against the real implementation.
usage: Triggers on its own when you ask for tests on web app code.
Can also be invoked by name when reviewing an existing suite.
notes: Part of the same official repo as frontend-design and canvas-design.

skill:wordpress-block-theming.author: Automattic
skill:wordpress-block-theming.summary: WordPress theme development with Full Site Editing (FSE) — blocks, `theme.json`, block templates and block patterns.
skill:wordpress-block-theming.whatItDoes: Use it when building or changing a modern WordPress theme (block-based, not classic PHP templates), or when configuring `theme.json` (palette, typography, spacing).
whenToUse: Building or changing a block-based WordPress theme (Full Site Editing).
Configuring theme.json — palette, typography, spacing.
Working with templates/*.html, parts/*.html, block patterns or custom blocks.
usage: Doesn't apply to classic PHP-only themes (index.php, header.php…).
notes: Official skill from the company behind WordPress.com and WooCommerce — the most direct source for block theming conventions.

ItemDescriptions.agent:auditor: Reviews a diff against the project rules — correctness, architecture, stack conventions and reuse — before merging. Use after closing a feature or before a deploy. Read-only: it reports findings, it doesn't fix them. For interface changes use frontend; for a security audit use security.
ItemDescriptions.agent:backend: Implements server logic, API endpoints, data access and migrations. Use it to delegate the backend half of a task so it runs alongside the main agent. Writes code and verifies with tests, typecheck or linter in a sandbox.
ItemDescriptions.agent:code-reviewer: Reviews a diff or PR against the project rules (correctness, security, architecture, stack conventions) before merging. Use after finishing a feature or before a deploy checklist. For interface changes use ui-reviewer. Read-only — it reports findings, it doesn't fix them.
ItemDescriptions.agent:debugger: Analyzes the root cause of a bug before touching code. Use when something is broken and it isn't clear why — it reproduces the problem, isolates the cause and proposes a minimal fix plan. It doesn't implement the fix.
ItemDescriptions.agent:docs-writer: Updates the project documentation (01-08 in /docs, ADRs, changelog) and drafts the commit message when closing a task or session. Use when finishing a feature or wrapping up a work session. It can edit /docs files, not source code.
ItemDescriptions.agent:explorer: Read-only search in projects that follow this kit's conventions — locates files, functions, routes or config, and knows where to look first (`.claude/skills/` for the rules, `/docs` 01-08 for decisions already made). Use it for "where is X" / "what files use Y" before touching code. Prefer it over the generic Explore agent when the project has `/docs` or rule skills installed. Fast and cheap — it edits nothing.
ItemDescriptions.agent:frontend: Implements interface — components, pages, styles, forms and UI states. Use it to delegate the frontend half of a task so it runs alongside the main agent. Writes code and verifies with build, typecheck or linter in a sandbox.
ItemDescriptions.agent:planner: Architecture and implementation planning for projects that follow this kit's conventions — it plans against the rules installed in `.claude/skills/` and the ADRs already recorded in `/docs/07_DECISIONS.md`, so nothing already decided gets re-decided. Use it before touching code on tasks that affect more than 3 files, have more than one valid architecture, or include irreversible decisions (migrations, schema changes, data deletion). Prefer it over the generic Plan agent when the project has `/docs` or rule skills installed. It neither writes nor edits code.
ItemDescriptions.agent:security: Deep security audit — OWASP, auth, API endpoints, input validation, uploads, secrets, CORS. Use before shipping features with auth, APIs or sensitive data to production, or when an explicit security review is requested. Read-only, it doesn't fix.
ItemDescriptions.agent:security-auditor: Deep security audit — OWASP, auth, API endpoints, input validation, uploads, secrets, CORS. Use before shipping features with auth, APIs or sensitive data to production, or when a security review is explicitly requested. Read-only, it doesn't fix.
ItemDescriptions.agent:test-writer: Writes tests for code that's already implemented and runs them until they pass. Use after closing a feature, to cover a bug that's already diagnosed, or when tests are explicitly requested. It writes test files only — it doesn't modify the code under test.
ItemDescriptions.agent:ui-reviewer: Reviews interface changes — accessibility, UI states, responsive, on-page SEO and visual consistency. Use when the diff touches components, pages, styles or markup. Complements code-reviewer, which covers logic and architecture but not UI. Read-only — it reports findings, it doesn't fix them.
ItemDescriptions.agents-md: Project rules in the open AGENTS.md standard — so any AI can pick the project up, not just Gemini.
ItemDescriptions.core: Global project memory: rules in AGENTS.md (readable by any AI) and CLAUDE.md, which imports them for Claude Code.
ItemDescriptions.database:mongodb: Documents, variable schema, high write volume.
ItemDescriptions.database:mysql: Relational — shared hosting / an existing LAMP stack.
ItemDescriptions.database:postgres: Relational, strong referential integrity — the recommended default.
ItemDescriptions.global:GEMINI.md: Always On global core — principles, base stack, naming, rule hierarchy.
ItemDescriptions.global:bug-fix.md: Something is broken — the AI finds the root cause first.
ItemDescriptions.global:deploy-checklist.md: Before shipping to production — a full checklist of code, security, UI and docs.
ItemDescriptions.global:grill.md: A structured interrogation to sharpen a plan before coding — the AI asks, you answer, and only then does planning start.
ItemDescriptions.global:new-feature.md: Before starting any new task — defines the plan, creates the git branch and updates 06_TASKS.md.
ItemDescriptions.global:security-audit.md: Use before shipping any feature with auth, APIs or sensitive data.
ItemDescriptions.global:session-close.md: At the end of the day or a task — checks docs and code, and drafts the suggested commit.
ItemDescriptions.global:tools-reference.md: Initial setup, or a reference for the available skills and tools and when to use each.
ItemDescriptions.rule:architecture: Trigger when creating a module, file or new feature, or when deciding which folder/layer a component, service or endpoint belongs in.
ItemDescriptions.rule:cms: Trigger when working with WordPress, Drupal or a headless CMS (Sanity, Contentful, Strapi) — hardening, API keys, webhooks.
ItemDescriptions.rule:operations: Trigger when setting up CI/CD, logging, external error/timeout handling, infrastructure, or when integrating an agent/LLM that runs tool calls.
ItemDescriptions.rule:pwa: Trigger only if the project is a PWA — manifest, service worker, cache strategies, offline state, update flow or installability.
ItemDescriptions.rule:security: Trigger when writing or reviewing authentication, API endpoints, input validation, uploads, secret handling, CORS, tracking/analytics cookies, consent or privacy compliance, or any code that receives data from the client.
ItemDescriptions.rule:seo: Trigger when working on meta tags, Open Graph, structured data, canonical, sitemap, or when diagnosing indexing, ranking and Core Web Vitals as an SEO factor.
ItemDescriptions.rule:stack-conventions: Language- and framework-specific conventions — applied automatically based on the extension of the file being edited.
ItemDescriptions.rule:ui-ux: Trigger when building or reviewing interfaces, visual components, forms, loading/error states, accessibility, dark mode or i18n/translations.
ItemDescriptions.skill:ai-seo: Optimization to get content cited by AI engines (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot) — AEO/GEO, llms.txt, agent-readable formatting. Use it when the ask is to get AI to cite the site, to improve visibility in AI-generated answers, or when "AI SEO", "AEO", "GEO", "llms.txt" or "zero-click search" come up. It complements seo-audit (classic technical SEO) rather than replacing it: one covers indexing and crawling, the other citability by LLMs.
ItemDescriptions.skill:api-security-best-practices: Implement secure API design patterns including authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, and protection against common API vulnerabilities.
ItemDescriptions.skill:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
ItemDescriptions.skill:domain-modeling: Use it while you work, not as a separate step: when a new or ambiguous domain term shows up, when two people (or the code and the conversation) mean different things by the same word, or when naming entities, tables, types and endpoints. Keeps the project glossary in `docs/CONTEXT.md` alive.
ItemDescriptions.skill:error-handling-patterns: Master error handling patterns across languages including exceptions, Result types, error propagation, and graceful degradation to build resilient applications. Use when implementing error handling, designing APIs, or improving application reliability.
ItemDescriptions.skill:fastapi: Official FastAPI best practices — triggers automatically when working on .py files that use FastAPI or Pydantic. Always current with the framework's latest versions and features.
ItemDescriptions.skill:frontend-design: Intentional aesthetic direction when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with typography, visual direction and the decisions that keep an interface from looking like a generic framework default ("AI slop"). Use it when starting any new UI in a project that already has a defined design system (brand brief, palette, typography) — the usual case at Orange Latam.
ItemDescriptions.skill:impeccable: A design vocabulary with 23 commands plus an anti-pattern audit. Use it when you need to audit, polish, critique or improve interfaces. Covers typography, color, motion, spacing, interaction, responsive and UX writing.
ItemDescriptions.skill:prisma-database-setup: Prisma's official guide to designing the schema, configuring the datasource and running migrations — PostgreSQL, MySQL and the rest of the supported providers. Use it when starting a Prisma project, when designing or changing the schema (`schema.prisma`), or when setting up migrations for the first time. Relevant for projects with a large relational PostgreSQL backend (a CRM with dozens of tables, say).
ItemDescriptions.skill:project-planning: Use it before coding a new project or a large initiative (touches more than 3 files, has more than one valid architecture, or includes an irreversible decision). Turns an already-validated idea into the planning documents in `/docs` this kit defines (`01_PROJECT_PRD.md` … `07_DECISIONS.md` + `09_TESTING.md`), in order, before any code gets written.
ItemDescriptions.skill:seo-audit: Audits, reviews or diagnoses SEO problems on the site — technical SEO, meta tags, page speed, Core Web Vitals, crawl/indexing errors, traffic or ranking drops. Use it when the ask is an SEO audit, a diagnosis of why something doesn't rank, or something vague like "check the SEO" or "help me with SEO". Diagnosis only — this project's concrete thresholds and specs live in .agents/rules/seo.md and win over any generic suggestion from the skill.
ItemDescriptions.skill:vercel-composition-patterns: React/Next.js component composition patterns — refactoring components with too many boolean props, designing reusable component APIs shadcn/ui-style (slots, compound components, render props instead of flags). Use it when you need to refactor a component that accumulated `is*`/`show*` props, or when designing the public API of a reusable component.
ItemDescriptions.skill:vercel-react-best-practices: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering. This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code to ensure optimal performance patterns. Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.
ItemDescriptions.skill:web-design-guidelines: Audits UI code against the Vercel Web Interface Guidelines. Use it when the ask is to review UI, check accessibility, audit design, review UX, or check compliance with interface standards.
ItemDescriptions.skill:wordpress-block-theming: WordPress theme development with Full Site Editing (FSE) — blocks, `theme.json`, block templates and block patterns. Use it when building or changing a modern WordPress theme (block-based, not classic PHP templates), or when configuring `theme.json` (palette, typography, spacing).

cambios: /subagentes now shows both catalogs (4 from Antigravity + 8 from Claude Code) in each tool's native format, and it also appears under the “Antigravity only” menu. It used to filter for claude-code alone.

Visual theme unified across the pages still on the old style: /subagentes, /mejores-skill, /skills-por-proyecto, /prompts and /plantillas. The ZIP builder, its preview modal (which opened with a white background on a dark site) and the templates download block were carrying the same leftovers.
The two skill views merged into one page: the flat catalog and the by-project-type grouping are now tabs on /mejores-skill. The old route redirects.
The data content of the site moved to messages/*.json: skills, prompt templates, stack labels, job types and this changelog are now translated instead of Spanish-only.

Language rule corrected to match reality: the core said “code always in English”, but the repo had 67 comments in Spanish against 15 in English. It now reads “identifiers and file names in English; comments and documentation in Spanish”. Translating everything was evaluated and dropped: 4 of the 14 packaged skills are third-party and in English, and Spanish runs only 3.8% longer than English in technical text.

Antigravity and Claude Code become fully independent kits: the hybrid mode is gone. No item belongs to both tools — the /docs templates, the external skills and the database add-on are emitted once per tool. Each ZIP is self-contained and doesn't assume you have the other agent installed.
The home page goes from 3 usage modes to 2, and /subagentes moves under the “Claude only” menu.
code-reviewer no longer promises to review UI/UX (its checklist never did): it now hands off to ui-reviewer.
explorer and planner spell out what sets them apart from the Explore and Plan agents Claude Code ships with: they know the /docs 01-08 convention and the rules installed in .claude/skills/.
Site interface reorganized: layout, nav, home and skill cards adjusted.
This changelog added (CHANGELOG.md + the /changelog page).
Nav labels normalized: the three generic “Home” entries replaced with descriptive labels, and a single-item group became a direct link.
/stacks and /stacks-app merged into a single /stacks page on the current visual theme.
The project starts using its own /docs convention to track work (06_TASKS.md and 07_DECISIONS.md).
/ becomes the hub index (usage modes, skill catalog and changelog); the Antigravity per-stack presets move to their own /antigravity page.
agregado: New SDD templates: 09_TESTING (how to run the tests and which test verifies each requirement) and 10_RUNBOOK (environments, deploy, rollback, monitoring and incidents). Requirements in 01_PROJECT_PRD now get an ID and verifiable acceptance criteria, and 06_TASKS opens with a handoff status so anyone can pick the project up.

Both kits ship an AGENTS.md at the project root: the open standard read by Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Antigravity, with the rules in a tool-neutral version and a project map (where the rules, skills and /docs live). If another AI picks the project up, it finds the same thing. In the Claude Code kit, CLAUDE.md imports it with @AGENTS.md.

The Claude Code kit as a native plugin: /plugin marketplace add luiskaco/-makeRuleIA installs the 9 rules as native skills, the 7 commands and the 8 subagents, and updates from git instead of staying frozen like the ZIP. Versioned by date (CalVer).

Four subagents for Antigravity: auditor and security (read-only) plus backend and frontend (which implement and verify their own work in a sandbox). Antigravity supports file-declared subagents — .agents/agents/<name>/agent.md — and the kit assumed that was impossible. They come preselected in all 8 Antigravity presets.

Two new subagents, from 6 to 8: ui-reviewer (accessibility, the 5 UI states, responsive, on-page SEO and consistency with the design system) and test-writer (detects the project's test framework instead of assuming it, and never modifies the code under test).
arreglado: A codebase-memory MCP config block, specific to the author's machine, was shipping inside the kits' GEMINI.md and CLAUDE.md. The generator now strips it.
The Claude Code commands weren't downloadable: all 6 existed and showed up in /build, but no preset preselected them, so the ZIP shipped without the .claude/commands/ folder.

code-reviewer pointed at .agents/rules/*, paths that don't exist in a Claude Code ZIP — those rules install as .claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md. It only worked if you had also downloaded the Antigravity ZIP.
Duplicated segments in every generated ZIP: docs/docs/… and .agents/.agents/…, which also didn't match the copy commands in the bundled INSTALL.md.

Antigravity-specific content leaking into Claude Code ZIPs: 00_GEMINI_START.md is no longer included in claude-code presets, and the stray references to GEMINI.md in shared files now point to CORE.md too.
quitado: The 00_GEMINI_START template is gone: the real stack, a different docs layout or rules that don't apply now go in the Project section of AGENTS.md, which any AI reads. If a project still has one, move its content there.
The “Antigravity + Claude” usage mode: its nav entry and its home card. The subagents are still there, under “Claude only”.
Empty placeholder pages with no nav link: /proximamente and /mejores-repos-utilidades.
